bib.title: Reproducible Scaling Laws for Contrastive Language-Image Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Reproducible scaling laws for contrastive language-image learning". Authors: Mehdi Cherti, Romain Beaumont, Ross Wightman, Mitchell Wortsman, Gabriel Ilharco, Cade Gordon, Christoph Schuhmann, Ludwig Schmidt, Jenia Jitsev (LAION, UC Berkeley, HuggingFace, U. Washington, Juelich Supercomputing Center). Venue: the PDF does not name a conference. It is stamped "arXiv:2212.07143v2 [cs.LG] 13 Jul 2024", so cite it as a preprint (arXiv v2, 2024; v1 Dec 2022). The filename says 2023. If you want a conference venue, it has to come from somewhere other than this PDF.

COVERAGE: Read all 107,916 of 107,916 chars (pp. 1–40). That covers the main text, the limitations, Appendix A (distributed training), and Appendix B with Tables 2–26, broader impact and author contributions. I skimmed the references only for origins.

CLAIMS
- claim: Zero-shot classification scales better with OpenAI's WIT-400M data than with LAION. Fit form is E = βC^α, where E is error and C is total compute in GMAC per sample × samples seen. The fit is on the Pareto frontier.
  number: ImageNet α_openCLIP −0.11 vs α_CLIP −0.16; robustness α −0.13 vs −0.24
  setup: Zero-shot top-1. OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 to g/14 on LAION-80M/400M/2B, 3B/13B/34B samples seen. OpenAI CLIP B/32, B/16, L/14 on WIT-400M. Compute axis is binned and the best model in each bin is kept. Robustness is the average over ImageNet-V2, R, Sketch, ObjectNet and A.
  quote: "we measure scaling coefficients αopenCLIP = −0.11 and αCLIP = −0.16 for zero-shot top-1 ImageNet and αopenCLIP = −0.13 and αCLIP = −0.24 for ImageNet robustness datasets performance"
  where: p.7
- claim: Zero-shot retrieval reverses this: LAION scales better than WIT.
  number: MS-COCO α_openCLIP −0.08 vs α_CLIP −0.05; Flickr30K −0.19 vs −0.10
  setup: Image retrieval, error = 100 − Recall@5. Karpathy test splits. Cosine similarity ranking.
  quote: "We measure scaling coefficientsαopenCLIP = −0.08 and αCLIP = −0.05 for zero-shot retrieval on MS-COCO andαopenCLIP = −0.19 and αCLIP = −0.10 for Flickr30K. In contrast to zero-shot accuracy, retrieval performance shows a scaling advantage for OpenCLIP pre-trained on LAION-400M/2B"
  where: p.7
- claim: The authors' hypothesis for the reversal is that LAION was filtered by CLIP ViT-B/32 image-text similarity, which may suit retrieval, while WIT's curation may lean toward ImageNet. They did not test this.
  number: none
  setup: The authors propose testing it by filtering with a stronger L/14 model.
  quote: "LAION-400M/2B was filtered by a pre-trained OpenAI ViT-B/32 model relying on its similarity measurements for image-text pairs, which may have rendered the dataset more suitable for retrieval based tasks"
  where: p.11
- claim: In the headline comparison, LAION-2B matches WIT on ImageNet at L/14 and is far ahead on COCO retrieval.
  number: CLIP WIT-400M L/14: 75.5 IN / 55.8 VTAB+ / 61.1 COCO; LAION-2B L/14: 75.2 / 54.6 / 71.1; LAION-2B H/14: 78.0 / 56.4 / 73.4
  setup: Zero-shot at 224 px. VTAB+ is the average of 35 datasets. COCO is image retrieval R@5.
  quote: "CLIP [55] WIT-400M L/14 75.5 55.8 61.1 Ours LAION-2B L/14 75.2 54.6 71.1 Ours LAION-2B H/14 78.0 56.4 73.4"
  where: p.2, Table 1
- claim: The best measured zero-shot ImageNet result is 78%, from ViT-H/14 on LAION-2B.
  number: 78% (77.97 in Table 19)
  setup: ViT-H/14, LAION-2B, 34B samples seen, the largest compute in the study.
  quote: "The strongest ImageNet accuracy (78%) is obtained with the largest total pre-training compute, using ViT-H/14 pre-trained on LAION-2B data scale and 34B samples seen."
  where: p.7
- claim: Best measured retrieval scores, all from H/14 on LAION-2B at 34B samples seen.
  number: COCO image R@5 73.43; COCO text R@5 86.04; Flickr image R@5 94.10; Flickr text R@5 99.30
  setup: Zero-shot.
  quote: "ViT-H/14 34B - - 73.43" (Table 21); "ViT-H/14 34B - - 86.04" (Table 22); "ViT-H/14 34B - - 94.10" (Table 23); "ViT-H/14 34B - - 99.30" (Table 24)
  where: pp.38–39
- claim: Bottlenecks. Small models see no gain from moving 400M to 2B data unless samples seen is large. L/14 on 400M stops improving from 13B to 34B samples seen.
  number: ImageNet zero-shot, B/32: 400M 64.06 vs 2B 66.47 at 34B seen; 63.23 vs 62.53 at 13B seen
  setup: Table 19.
  quote: "OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 and ViT-B/16 models show no change or deterioration of performance when increasing data scale from 400M to 2B when using a smaller samples seen scale (3B or 13B)"; Table 19 "ViT-B/32 ... 13B 56.46 63.23 62.53 34B 56.43 64.06 66.47"
  where: p.7; p.37
- claim: Extrapolated predictions. These are predicted, not measured.
  number: g/14 at 2B data and 34B seen: 79.1%. At 68B seen: H/14 79.7%, g/14 80.7%, G/14 81.9% ImageNet. G/14 at 68B: 76.99 COCO R@5.
  setup: Pareto-frontier power-law fit. In Table 4 only rows marked * are measured.
  quote: "assuming 68B samples seen we estimate top-1 accuracies of 79.7%, 80.7%, and 81.9% for ViT-H/14, ViT-g/14 and ViT-G/14"; "G/14 (68B samples seen), we predict 81.92% zero-shot top-1 accuracy on ImageNet and 76.99% image retrieval Recall@5 on MS-COCO"
  where: p.7; p.23
- claim: Linear probes also follow power laws on ImageNet, CIFAR-100 (10-shot, 25-shot and full) and VTAB. CLIP-WIT keeps an edge on ImageNet probes at matched scale.
  number: Full ImageNet probe: L/14 13B CLIP-WIT 84.39; L/14 13B LAION-400M 81.77; H/14 34B LAION-2B 84.85
  setup: Features cached, no augmentation. Softmax regression with Adam, batch 256, sweep over lr and epochs. Fig. 2 fit: E = 7.68·C^−0.13 (OpenCLIP) vs 34.38·C^−0.20 (CLIP). The extraction drops the minus sign.
  quote: "ViT-L/14 13B CLIP-WIT 73.77 73.51 77.67 84.39"; "ViT-H/14 34B LAION-2B 75.96 75.79 79.07 84.85"
  where: pp.8–9, p.28 Table 5
- claim: ImageNet fine-tuning of OpenCLIP encoders reaches 82.6–88.5% top-1.
  number: 82.6–88.5%; best is H/14 at 336 px, IN-12k intermediate, 88.50
  setup: timm. Encoders from the 2B-data, 34B-seen runs. Either direct fine-tuning or ImageNet-12k first.
  quote: "The OpenCLIP models range from 82.6 to 88.5% top-1 on ImageNet"
  where: p.9; Table 9 p.29
- claim: Compute. Up to 1520 A100s. The whole study used about 1.06M GPU-hours and 370 MWh. H/14 alone took 229,665 GPU-h.
  number: Total 1058318 GPU-h / 370.41 MWh
  setup: JUWELS Booster plus Stability AI. Global batch 86–88K.
  quote: "H/14 LAION-2B 96(79104) 5e-4 2K 34B 824 279 229665/80.38"; "Total 1058318/370.41"
  where: p.36 Table 18
- claim: Control experiments show the trends are not artefacts. Batch size moves results by 0.2–0.5%. Trial-to-trial variance is about 0.1%. A 400M subset of LAION-2B matches LAION-400M (63.56 vs 63.37).
  number: 0.2–0.5%; ~0.1%
  setup: B/32 (and B/16 and L/14 for the batch control), LAION-400M, 13B samples seen.
  quote: "observe a difference of0.2 − 0.5% across different settings"; "The result suggests a small variance of around 0.1%"
  where: p.5; p.31
- claim: Test-set duplicates in LAION are around 1%, higher for ImageNet-R and Sketch. Removing them barely changes accuracy.
  number: ImageNet-R 3.80%, Sketch 5.15%; ImageNet-R accuracy 89.32 to 89.21
  setup: pHash DCT against LAION-400M, H/14.
  quote: "Overall, the ratio of detected duplicates is around 1%, except on ImageNet-R (3.80%) and ImageNet-Sketch (5.15%)"
  where: p.21
- claim: Large models hit loss spikes under fp16. Switching to bfloat16 fixed it.
  number: none
  setup: L/14, H/14, g/14.
  quote: "We fixed the issue by switching from mixed precision with float16 to mixed precision with bfloat16."
  where: p.6
- claim: The class-vs-retrieval pattern also holds for OpenAI's ResNet CLIPs.
  number: CLIP ResNet ImageNet fit C^−0.13, COCO C^−0.05
  setup: Fig. 12.
  quote: "both OpenAI's ResNets and ViT trained on WIT demonstrate stronger scaling on zero-shot classification but worse scaling on retrieval than openCLIP trained on LAION datasets"
  where: p.32

LIMITS: The authors concede that the scale space is sampled sparsely, that there was no full hyperparameter tuning at large scale, and that there are only 3 OpenAI CLIP points (B/32, B/16, L/14) because WIT is private. The duplicate check is simple. H/14 and g/14 each have only one configuration. The data explanation for the WIT/LAION difference is a hypothesis; it is not isolated experimentally. The study does not give compute-optimal (Chinchilla-style) allocation and does not separate vision and text encoder scaling; both are listed as future work. Extrapolations are predictions, and the authors warn of saturation. The predicted 79.1% sits below the private-data systems BASIC 85.7, LiT 85.2 and CoCa 86.1. The study covers contrastive dual encoders only, and zero-shot results are at 224 px. What has dated: LAION-5B was later withdrawn by LAION for content-safety review, a fact not in this PDF that should be checked. Newer data-curation work (DataComp, MetaCLIP, SigLIP) postdates the paper. Code and models are described as "will be available".

BUILDS ON: CLIP (Radford et al. [55], 2021); ALIGN (Jia et al. [33], 2021); Kaplan et al. scaling laws [35] (2020); Hoffmann et al. compute-optimal [28] (2022); Zhai et al. Scaling ViTs [82] (2022); Hestness et al. [26] (2017); LAION-400M [65] (2021) and LAION-5B [64] (NeurIPS 2022 D&B); OpenCLIP (Ilharco et al. [32], 2021); InfoNCE (Oord et al. [52], 2018); WiSE-FT patching (Ilharco et al. [31], 2022); BASIC [54], LiT [84], CoCa [80].

CODE: There is no code listing. One method detail matters for the notes on sharded contrastive loss. Before sharding, the full N×N similarity matrix "totalling to 4 GB of VRAM in FP32"; after sharding, with local batch 256, it takes "64 MB". Gradients need "torch.distributed.nn.functional.all_gather" because "PyTorch's standardtorch.distributed.all_gather can not be differentiated through" (pp.19–20).

FIGURES:
- Fig. 1 (p.3). Compute vs zero-shot ImageNet and robustness error (1a), and COCO and Flickr retrieval error (1b), with the OpenCLIP and CLIP fit lines. The opposite slopes for classification and retrieval are visible at a glance. This is the best figure for both target notes.
- Fig. 8 (p.23). Extrapolation to H/14, g/14 and G/14 at 68B samples seen, for ImageNet and COCO. Shows what a prediction from a scaling law looks like.
- Fig. 2 (p.8). Linear probe scaling on ImageNet and CIFAR-100, few-shot and full.
- Fig. 12 (p.33). The ResNet CLIP control, showing the effect is not tied to the architecture.
- Fig. 6 (p.20). DDP scaling efficiency, 84.35% at 1024 GPUs. Optional.

PROBLEMS: The text extraction drops minus signs and superscripts in the fit labels inside figures, so "E = 5.86 * C 0.11" really means C^−0.11. The body text on p.7 gives the signed values, so quote from there. Some words run together (e.g. "pretrainedonLAION-400M/2B"). The PDF contains no embedded instructions. No venue is printed.
